q: How much CO2 does a Khurja pottery unit save moving its kiln from coal to gas?
title: Khurja pottery: coal to gas saving
short: Per unit of heat, natural gas emits about 40% less CO2 than bituminous coal under IPCC defaults: 56.1 against 94.6 kg CO2 per GJ. The real saving also depends on kiln efficiency, so compare fuel bills before and after for the same output.
audience: Ceramic and pottery units in the Khurja cluster of Uttar Pradesh

ul: Coal (other bituminous): 94.6 kg CO2 per GJ (IPCC 2006 default).
Natural gas: 56.1 kg CO2 per GJ.

p: A gas kiln often fires more efficiently, which adds to the saving. Use measured fuel per tonne fired before and after, not the factor alone.

example.title: Worked example: same heat (illustrative quantity)
lines: Heat needed: 258 GJ (about 10 t of coal at 25.8 GJ per t)
example.note: Heat demand is illustrative and assumes equal kiln efficiency.

senseible: Senseible reads electricity bills (CEA grid factor 0.710 kg CO2 per kWh, CO2 Baseline Database version 21.0) and diesel, LPG and gas invoices (IPCC 2006 defaults) into a dated, fingerprinted Scope 1 and 2 record for each site. Intensity per unit uses the activity count you enter, and estimates are labelled as estimates.
